newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Golf-Norman suffers in wild weather.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Golf-Norman suffers in wild weather.

text.p: World number one Greg Norman suffered badly in wild weather on Friday to be five shots off the lead after the second round of the tournament he is hosting. Norman, who is playing in his final tournament before taking a three-month break to recuperate from a back problem, shot a three-over-par 75 to well back on 144.
Dutch golfer Rolf Muntz, Jerry Kelly of the United States, New Zealand's Elliot Boult and Lucas Parsons of Australia shared the halfway lead of the Greg Norman Classic on five-under 139.
Muntz and Parsons both shot 72 after opening with rounds of 67 at the par-72 Royal Melbourne course. Boult carded a second round 70 and Kelly a 69.
Michael Long of New Zealand was two shots behind the leaders after a steady 71, with a group of six players a further shot behind.

Norman had been two shots off the overnight pace after an opening round of 69 and had dropped another two shots by the time he reached the ninth tee, only for a fierce storm to drive players from the course.

The Australian then bogeyed the par-four ninth when players returned to the course an hour later and went on to triple bogey the final hole. Norman declined to be interviewed and will start the third round even with the card.
Among those who missed the halfway cut were European and U.S. Tour regulars Rodger Davis and Wayne Grady and former Classic champion Anthony Gilligan, all of Australia.
